correctness.rationale: For any contiguous partition let z be blockwise constant with strict boundary gaps, choose strictly positive multipliers on internal edges and zero on boundary edges, and put m_i(x_i−z_i)=λ_i−λ_{i−1}. This is the stationarity sign for z_i−z_{i+1}≤0; the block means, prefix-sum multipliers and gaps vary continuously so the partition persists on an open neighborhood. On the quotient by constants, the step functions identify the seminorm with weighted ℓ1, giving the maximum step-column gain. A step inside (p,q] becomes the constant (T_q−T_j)/(T_q−T_p) on that block; the two edge jumps give exactly the chord's height (with zero artificial boundary weights). Taking the max over attainable partitions gives the upper hull at every knot by the two-support extreme point of the fixed-barycenter linear program. Finite continuous piecewise linearity yields the global bound by summing segment increments, including segments in chamber boundaries where the neighboring restrictions agree. A sufficiently small step in a maximizing chamber attains the bound; an identity chamber is allowed when the factor is 1. Concavity and minimal stabilizing enlargement follow from hull minimality. The two sample constants and 558 exact additional input pairs agreed with an independent upper-hull and weighted max–min computation: python3 /workspace/reproductions/3.py. This calculation is supplementary; the general proof is not inferred from it.
